verdict_reason: Drove the real evaluate() on gpt2/distilgpt2/pythia-70m at the package default (num_samples=20, WikiText) and reproduced EVERY figure in the 2026-09-05 ledger table to the quoted digits: gpt2 mean_persistence_h0 9.655929 -> 63.918390 (+562.0%), max_persistence_h0 13.533708 -> 82.327766, mean_persistence_h1 0.539361 -> 1.835098, mean_persistence_h0_norm 0.417046 -> 0.730877; distilgpt2 7.949954 -> 50.032558; pythia-70m 19.469393 -> 6.008640 (-69.1%) and its norm 0.782120 -> 0.681369. The persistence kernel itself is a textbook Vietoris-Rips summary computed by ripser: _lifespan_summary drops the essential infinite H0 bar and averages death-birth, which I checked against a hand-built diagram. The depth-aligned rename is real: the live gpt2 output has 39 feature keys, all first/mid/last_layer_*, with the 47 absolute-index keys moved under _meta_.
comparable_reason: Persistence is a metric-space statistic in unnormalised hidden-state units, so the raw summaries are not comparable across models: archive rho for layer_0_mean_persistence_h0 is -0.040 (d_model) / +0.141 (n_layers) / +0.188 (log vocab), but it is rho +0.98-1.00 with layer_0_mean_pairwise_distance, which is itself an arbitrary scale. The MPD-normalised twin trades that for a width association (archive layer_0_mean_persistence_h0_norm +0.238 d_model / +0.147 n_layers / +0.203 log params). Both families are emitted as first-class features, so a selector sees the raw and the normalised halves of the same degree of freedom side by side.
github_repo: scikit-tda/ripser.py; GUDHI (engines). Zomorodian-Carlsson 2005 and Edelsbrunner-Harer 2008 released no code.
github_reason: ripser.py is the engine BLME calls, not an independent reference for the estimand. No reference implementation of 'persistent homology of LM hidden states' exists to compare against; the summary layer (_lifespan_summary, _scale_stratified_summary) is BLME's own design and is anchored only on constructed diagrams.
paper_reason: The persistence summary is exact against an analytically known diagram (unit square: H0 mean = max = 1, one H1 bar of persistence sqrt(2)-1), which is the only closed form available. Naitzat et al. 2020, cited as motivation, publishes Betti-number curves for synthetic manifolds under 2,600-11,250 points, nothing reproducible from 20 mean-pooled sentence vectors. Fay et al. arXiv:2505.20435, cited for the fine/coarse split, uses 64 subsamples of 4,096 points and a 41-dimensional barcode vector and does not define BLME's death < 0.5*MPD threshold.
confounds_reason: The raw persistence family is dominated by the point cloud's own scale (mean pairwise distance) rather than by depth or width; the normalised family trades that for rho +0.238 with d_model on the archive. Separately, _meta_h1_resolves_between_models is False at both the package (20) and study (50) sample sizes, and reads False on all six of my runs, i.e. the task itself declares its H1 family unusable for cross-model ordering at the shipped N.
defects: h1_fine_persistence_frac is NaN when a layer has NO H1 bars while mean_persistence_h1 is 0.0 in the same situation. Verified directly on a diagram with an empty H1 array: _scale_stratified_summary returns {'h1_fine_count': 0, 'h1_coarse_count': 0, 'h1_fine_persistence_frac': nan}. Unfixed from the previous round; it makes 'no loops' and 'loops of zero persistence' the same value in one key and a non-finite feature in another, and json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) then raises. None of my six runs hit it (all three models had >= 1 H1 bar at N=20), so it is intermittent per model and layer, which is worse.

Raw and MPD-normalised summaries are BOTH first-class feature keys: last_layer_mean_persistence_h0 = 63.918390 alongside last_layer_mean_persistence_h0_norm = 0.730877, and the same for max_persistence_h0 and mean_persistence_h1. Of the 39 feature keys 6 are the scale-confounded halves of another 6, and the denominator (mean_pairwise_distance) is correctly _meta_ while both numerator families are not.

num_loops_h1 counts every finite H1 bar with no persistence threshold, so it is unstable under arbitrarily small perturbations, and the fine/coarse split thresholds a bar's DEATH rather than its persistence -- a bar of lifetime 5e-05 that dies late is classified 'coarse'.

CONFIG: num_samples is 20 (package default) / 50 (study configs/tasks.yaml). load_default_corpus returns CONSECUTIVE WikiText passages, so at 20 the point cloud is 20 mean-pooled vectors drawn from ONE article. The same defaults.yaml edit raised topology_betti_curve and topology_persistence_entropy to 1000 and left homology (and persistence_landscape) at 20.
